absent: Encoding and full permission semantics of statistic descriptor modes beyond write-bit gating for debug files.
Locking and lifetime rules for per-VCPU iteration inside per-VCPU statistic aggregation.
Effects of arch VCPU load, put, PMI guest test, kernel test, and address retrieval beyond call pairing.
Registration site and lifetime of perf guest callbacks and handling of null PT and mediated hooks.
Layout and lifetime of kvm, vcpu, and statistic descriptor structures beyond the offsets accessed here.
Provider behavior and failure modes of dynamically resolved VFIO helpers beyond absent-symbol defaults.
Semantics of SPAPR TCE attach and release for IOMMU groups and table descriptors.
Arch noncoherent DMA register and unregister effects and idempotency requirements.
Semantics of bypass connect and disconnect operations and layout of producer, consumer, and table entries.
Error precedence and retry behavior when bypass producer insertion collides with an existing key.

findings.text: Per-VM statistics are read and cleared by applying a byte displacement inside the VM-wide counters area, while per-VCPU statistics derive the same displacement inside each VCPU counters area, summing across all VCPUs on read and zeroing each VCPU on clear.

Statistic clear operations accept only a zero value and otherwise fail as invalid, while dispatch on an unrecognized statistic category fails as a fault; global clear helpers enforce the same zero-only rule before walking VMs.

Global aggregation helpers that sum or reset one statistic offset across every VM acquire the global VM list mutex for the whole walk and release it afterwards, returning success after the protected traversal.

Opening a per-VM debug statistics file first acquires a safe reference on the owning VM and fails as missing when the VM is gone; the reference is released if attribute setup fails and otherwise held until the file release hook drops it.

A per-VM statistics file operations table routes open through a decimal unsigned formatting check plus the shared debug open path, routes release through the shared release path, and delegates transfer to generic simple attribute read and write handlers.

A VCPU moves between scheduled-in and scheduled-out states via scheduler hooks: entry clears preempted and ready markers, publishes the VCPU as the current CPU occupant, invokes arch load, then clears the scheduled-out marker; exit sets scheduled-out, conditionally sets preempted and ready when the task remains runnable and the VCPU wants to run, then invokes arch put and clears the CPU occupant.

Conversion from scheduler notifier to VCPU uses container lookup around the embedded notifier member, and the per-CPU current VCPU pointer is written on every sched-in and cleared on every sched-out paired with arch load and put calls.
A global accessor exposes the address of the per-CPU variable that tracks the currently running VCPU, allowing other subsystems to observe the occupant on each CPU.

Perf guest state reports inactive when the current VCPU is outside PMI guest context, otherwise reports active and additionally marks user mode when the VCPU is not in kernel context; address retrieval warns and yields zero when called outside PMI guest context and otherwise delegates to arch.
The perf guest callback table wires a state hook and an address hook to the KVM implementations described above while leaving Intel PT and mediated PMI hooks empty.

Page-follow parameters bundle a memory slot pointer, guest frame number, host virtual address, lookup modifier flags, a pin request for kernel writable mappings, an optional writable-mapping output, and an optional refcounted page output that is only populated for refcounted or pinned pages.

VFIO attachment state keeps per-file entries linked together, each holding a file reference and optionally an IOMMU group on SPAPR builds, plus device-wide state with an entry list, a mutex, and a cached noncoherent flag.

KVM resolves VFIO helper entry points dynamically on each use and treats lookup failure as absent capability: association becomes a no-op, validity and enforced-coherency checks report false, and group lookup yields null.

Coherency state is recomputed by scanning attached files for any entry lacking enforced coherency; only a change in the aggregate flag triggers arch registration or unregistration for noncoherent DMA.

Adding a file validates the descriptor, rejects non-VFIO descriptors as invalid, rejects duplicates as already present, allocates and links a new entry with an extra file reference, associates the VM, and refreshes coherency; removal looks up by file identity, detaches and frees on match, refreshes coherency, and reports missing when absent; freeing on SPAPR also releases any attached IOMMU group before clearing association, dropping the reference, unlinking, and deallocating.

All VFIO file list mutations and scans in add, remove, and SPAPR attach paths execute under the device private mutex via scoped acquisition, while device creation requires the owning VM lock to be already held as checked by lock validation.

SPAPR TCE attachment copies a group-plus-table parameter from user space, validates the group descriptor, finds the matching attached file under lock, lazily resolves and caches its IOMMU group with an I/O error if resolution fails unexpectedly, then attaches that group to the named table and reports missing when no entry matches.

VFIO device attribute handling accepts only the file group, dispatching add and remove plus SPAPR TCE attach where configured by reading a small integer descriptor from user space, and capability probing succeeds for exactly those operations; all other groups or operations fail as not supported.

VFIO device creation rejects a second instance on the same VM as busy, initializes an empty file list and mutex, and stores private state; release walks and frees every remaining entry, refreshes coherency once more, then deallocates private state and the device object itself.

Interrupt-bypass producer registration and unregistration serialize global producer and consumer table access under a single file-local mutex held for lookup, insertion or erasure, and connect or disconnect decisions.

A bypass producer is keyed by the identity of its event object, records its interrupt number, is inserted into the producer table, synchronously connects when a consumer with the same key already exists with rollback of the insertion on connect failure, and on unregister disconnects from any linked consumer, removes its table entry, and clears its association; unregister with no association is a no-op and double binding is rejected as invalid.

Several paths warn on unexpected state without changing the primary error result: retrieving guest address outside guest context, releasing a SPAPR entry with no cached group, failing to resolve an expected IOMMU group, mismatched table erasure on producer teardown, and related one-time diagnostics.
Two header guard macros mark inclusion protection for the KVM MM-internal header and the KVM VFIO header.

Debug statistic files expose decimal unsigned values with newline termination and enable their write handler only when the descriptor mode carries write permission bits, so read-only descriptors reject clear attempts at the attribute layer before reaching the zero-check.
